# Jacob Lavoie

> Applied Research Scientist at Mila — Quebec AI Institute, working at the interface of neuroscience and computer engineering ("putting brains in computers, and computers in brains"). Research focus: neuro-AI at the hardware/algorithm boundary — retinal prosthetics, spiking and neuromorphic neural networks, model-based reinforcement learning and world models, and biomedical machine learning.

Jacob Lavoie is trained in both neuroscience and computer engineering and works at the interface of the two. He is especially interested in the ergonomic and security dimensions of AI-leveraged human–machine interfaces (brain–computer interfaces, neurotech). MSc, Université de Sherbrooke (2023). Based in Montréal, Québec, Canada.

## Selected publications
- Learning to See via Epiretinal Implant Stimulation in silico with Model-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning — Biomedical Physics & Engineering Express 10(2), 025006 (2024). https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03118
- Affective Music Recommendation: A Rollout-Based World Model for Offline Preference Optimization — arXiv:2605.28810 (2026).
- A 1.6-fJ/Spike Subthreshold Analog Spiking Neuron in 28nm CMOS — NEWCAS 2022. https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07734
- Quantized spiking neural networks on FPGA for retinal prosthetics — BioCAS 2023.
- Energy-efficient spiking neural network for a retinal prosthesis — Neuroelectronics 2(1) (2025).
